texts: mixed: the group-level facts are right (the keepers, the lanterns, sundown, day 300 of Year 1), but the parse also adds a per-member rule saying every single keeper lit the whole set of lanterns, which is more than your sentence claims. Marking the action as joint blocks that rule and keeps the reading you want: "On day 300 of Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row together lit the lanterns of the Harbor Row at sundown." Separately, "day 300 of Year 1" is stored as a plain day number, which the instruction set defines as a day-of-month, so a day-of-year index is indistinguishable from a day-of-month - no wording fixes that, it is just worth knowing.
good. the lanterns are correctly carried over from the previous sentence, and the per-member rule (each lantern burned mire-essence) is fireable and says nothing the sentence does not.

mixed: the group-level event is right, but the parse also adds a rule saying each individual lantern produced that one body of mist-light, over-stating what you wrote. Writing it as a joint act drops the over-asserting rule: "The lanterns together produced mist-light."
good. the mist-light, the nightmoths as a set, and the attracting event are all covered, with no invented extras.
good. the crowd is typed as a crowd whose members are nightmoths, and gathering is treated as one act of the whole crowd, so nothing is wrongly attributed to individual moths.
good. the three sky-cats with their count, the cliff-spires as the source of the descent, and a fireable per-member rule.
good. the hunt ties the three sky-cats to the nightmoth crowd already introduced and records the Harbor Row as where it happened.
good. the crowd is correctly the thing that undergoes the shrinking, and "at the Harbor Row" is attached to the crowd itself rather than to the shrinking.
good. this comes out as a fireable rule - any nightmoth that survived that particular hunt flees to the Hollows - with "each" recorded and the hunt bound to the hunting event of the earlier sentence.

mixed: the gaining, the Hollows lanterns, the threads and the "that night" dating are all right, but the added per-member rule says each lantern gained the whole bundle of threads. Marking it as joint keeps the collective reading and drops that rule: "The lanterns at the Hollows together gained silken threads that night."

mixed: the molting, the three sky-cats and the "during the hunt" link are all captured, but the parse makes the cats the volitional doer of the molting, where the instruction set treats the subject of an internal change of state as the one undergoing it - so the role is distorted. No wording controls that label directly; if you want the syntax to settle it, "During the hunt, the three sky-cats shed their feathers." is a transitive clause in which the cats are licensed as the doer.
good. the feathers, the falling, the base as the destination and the base-of-the-cliff part link are all there, with the feathers correctly the thing that falls rather than an actor.

bad: two things go wrong here - the bare plural "Nightmoths" mints a brand-new set of moths with no link to the crowd that gathered and was hunted at the Harbor Row, and the per-member rule then says each of those moths left the whole bundle of threads on the whole set of lanterns. Naming the crowd fixes both at once, because a singular collective subject is predicated as one unit and is never distributed to its members: "The nightmoth crowd left silken threads on the lanterns of the Harbor Row." The parse also treats the threads as changed by the leaving when they are merely deposited unchanged, but that is a role label your wording cannot control.

mixed: the collecting, the threads, the lanterns, dawn and day 301 are all recorded, but the per-member rule says each keeper collected the whole bundle of threads from every lantern. Marking the joint action drops it: "The keepers of the Harbor Row together collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 301 of Year 1." The day-of-year caveat noted on the first sentence applies to "day 301 of Year 1" here as well.
